overview: The Karnataka Startup Policy is a state-level initiative launched by the Government of Karnataka to foster innovation and entrepreneurship within the state. It aims to create a conducive ecosystem for startups by providing financial incentives, infrastructure support, regulatory simplification, and access to markets and mentorship. The policy focuses on sector-agnostic growth with special emphasis on technology-driven and social impact startups. It operates under the Department of IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka.
objectives: To promote innovation and entrepreneurship across Karnataka
To generate 6 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities
To achieve INR 50,000 Crore in economic output from startups by 2025
To establish at least one startup incubator in each district
To promote women, SC/ST, differently abled, and rural entrepreneurship
To develop sector-specific startup parks and innovation zones
To simplify regulatory compliance and provide single-window clearance
eligibility: Startups incorporated as Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm under Indian laws, having their primary place of business in Karnataka, recognized by DPIIT or certified by the Karnataka State Startup Committee, working on innovative products, services, or processes with potential for scalability and employment generation, and not formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business.
benefits: Financial support through seed funding, marketing assistance, and reimbursement of patent and certification costs; non-financial benefits include access to incubation centers, mentorship from industry experts, participation in national and international startup events, priority in government procurement, access to shared infrastructure and labs, regulatory facilitation through single-window clearance, and assistance in fundraising and investor connect.
financial_support: The policy provides seed support of up to INR 50 lakhs per startup in the form of grant or convertible debt, reimbursement of up to INR 2 lakhs for patent filing and INR 1 lakh for certification costs, marketing assistance of up to INR 5 lakhs for participation in approved events, and monthly operational support of INR 1 lakh per month for up to 12 months for startups in recognized incubators. Financial assistance is disbursed through nodal agencies and incubators after due diligence checks.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakhs as seed support per startup
application_process: 1. Register the startup on the Karnataka Startup Cell portal (startup.karnataka.gov.in). 2. Obtain DPIIT recognition or certification from the Karnataka State Startup Committee. 3. Apply for specific benefits (seed funding, marketing, patent reimbursement, etc.) through the online portal. 4. Submit required documents including incorporation certificate, DPIIT recognition, business plan, and financial projections. 5. Application is reviewed by the Karnataka State Startup Committee or designated nodal agency. 6. Upon approval, enter into an agreement and submit bank details for disbursement. 7. Funds are released in tranches based on milestones or as per the scheme guidelines.
required_documents: DPIIT recognition certificate or Karnataka State Startup Committee certification
Bank account details of the startup
Proof of primary place of business in Karnataka (e.g., utility bill, rental agreement)
Patent or certification invoices (for reimbursement claims)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Department of IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
caveats: Financial support is subject to availability of funds under the annual budget allocation
Startups must maintain primary operations in Karnataka for a minimum of 3 years after receiving support
Funding is disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement or audit compliance
Benefits under the policy cannot be combined with similar state-level incentives for the same expenditure
The policy is valid until 2025 unless extended by the Government of Karnataka
